dedupe_keys.name: hong kong catalogue of slopes and landslide incident locations cedd with the hko landslip warning database

description: The Civil Engineering and Development Department of Hong Kong publishes two open datasets on slope safety through DATA.GOV.HK and the CSDI Portal: the registered man-made slopes in the Catalogue of Slopes, updated monthly, and the location of landslide incidents, updated yearly, each with an API. Its slope safety website describes the Slope Information System behind the catalogue, with the works technical circular on registering and updating the catalogue, notes and an Excel form for registering slope features, notes on toe and crest facilities, applications for information from the catalogue, and a database program for computing scores under the New Priority Ranking Systems. The Hong Kong Observatory keeps a searchable database of landslip warnings from 1983, with provisional records shown since 10 October 2011 and confirmed within a working day. Access is free under the DATA.GOV.HK terms and conditions; no open licence is named. Caveats: the registered slopes are man-made features only, the incident dataset gives locations, not full reports, and the warning database is in Chinese on the page read. Coverage is Hong Kong. It supports hazard exposure and fragility analysis of roads, buildings and water mains near slopes during rainstorms, and validation of landslide models; related records are the Nepal landslide hazard maps of METEOR and the Catterline slope protection field data.
